title: 25.1 A Physics-Inspired Oscillator-Based Mixed-Signal Optimization Engine for Solving 50-Variable 218-Clause 3-SAT Problems with 100% Solvability and 31.7μs Solution Time
problem: Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solving is NP-complete; existing hardware solvers are limited to small problem sizes (<20 variables), suffer from long solution times (ms-level), or require complex problem embedding with high preprocessing overhead.
motivation: Efficient SAT solving enables breakthroughs in optimization, AI, cryptography, and hardware/software verification, motivating specialized hardware acceleration.
method: The engine uses coupled oscillators—electronic devices that swing back and forth and naturally synchronize with each other—to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (finding values for multiple true-or-false variables that satisfy a set of logical rules). Each variable and rule maps to an oscillator; the oscillators all interact at once in a continuous physical system, and their synchronized state naturally encodes which variable values satisfy all rules. This all-at-once approach, driven by physics rather than step-by-step logic, is much faster than traditional search. The hardware achieves 100% success on 50-variable, 218-clause problems in 31.7 microseconds.
key_novelty: All-to-all coupled oscillators directly solve Boolean satisfiability problems without complex preprocessing, achieving 50-variable solvability.
contributions: 50-variable 3-SAT solving (2.5x larger than prior oscillator-based approaches)
100% solution solvability on benchmark clauses with 31.7μs solution time
All-to-all variable connectivity enabling real-world high-fanout problem instances
baselines: prior physics-inspired oscillator solvers (20 variables, ms-scale)
digital SAT solver arrays with embedded preprocessing
limitations: Scalability beyond 50 variables and practical deployment on real cryptographic instances not discussed.
